Hi Andrew, I think you should be able to do something like this:
  gridsterItem(class='foo')

-Winston

On Tue, May 28, 2013 at 7:22 PM, Andrew Clark <scott.r...@gmail.com> wrote:
I can see that the dimensions of the gridsterItem (although not other values ?) can be changed in CSS

gridster .gs_w 
  border-radius: 5px; 
   width: 50px; /* works */
  background-color: #999fff; /* but not this */

}

I would like to set 
.gridster .gs_w.large { 
 
  width: 250px; 
}

but am not sure how to refer to this in the ui,
I have tried without success

gridsterItem(col = 2, row = 1, sizex = 1, sizey = 2,
                 tags$div(class = 'large'),
                 h4("NHL"),
      tableOutput("nhl")
    )

On Thursday, 23 May 2013 12:00:38 UTC-7, Andrew Clark wrote:
Great.  I look forward to that and working with rCharts in the future

On Thursday, 23 May 2013 10:14:17 UTC-7, Ramnath Vaidyanathan wrote:
Andrew,

I am reworking the dashboard example using rCharts, which supports HighCharts directly. This would allow you to customize all aspects of the plot including the tooltip and the y-axis limits dynamically, using R code, not needing to manipulate the javascript directly.

I will post my reworked example soon.

Best,
Ramnath


On Wednesday, May 22, 2013 6:33:41 PM UTC-4, Andrew Clark wrote:
So you hard-coded the scale and tootip somewhere?

On Wednesday, 22 May 2013 13:44:05 UTC-7, Winston Chang wrote:
Hi Andrew - sorry, I'm a Highcharts novice myself, so I can't be of much help on that front.

-Winston


On Wed, May 22, 2013 at 2:52 PM, Andrew Clark <scott.r...@gmail.com> wrote:
Winston
  Now that I have this up and running, I would like to play around with it a bit. On the highcharts front how would I go about amending the y axis on the fly
depending on the values being received e.g if they were stock quotes around 30 then the example range of 0-150 would not be appropriate. I'm also interested in changing tooltip etc. I'm guessing I could refer to the highcharts documentation but could do with an example of how to do this with shiny
cheers
andrew clark


On Friday, 17 May 2013 15:42:45 UTC-7, Winston Chang wrote:
Hi everyone - I've posted an app that demonstrates how to integrate Shiny with various Javascript libraries. It makes an interactive dashboard:
http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winstontest/shiny-jsdemo/

Source code (and information on how it's made):
https://github.com/wch/shiny-jsdemo

-Winston
